etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Medieval Latin allocāte, imperative of Latin allocāre, from ad- (“to”) + locus (“place”).

definitions.definition: To set aside for a purpose.

quote.citation: 2024 January 10, Chris Gilson, “RAIL's famous five...”, in RAIL, number 1000, page 27:
quote.text: By March 1994, it had moved to Cardiff Canton, and was still allocated there when its nameplates were taken off in March 1997.

definitions.definition: To distribute according to a plan, generally followed by the adposition to.
(computing) To reserve a portion of memory for use by a computer program.

quote.citation: 2011, José M. Garrido, Richard Schlesinger, Kenneth Hoganson, Principles of Modern Operating Systems, 2nd edition, Jones & Bartlett Publishers, →ISBN, page 264:
quote.text: The memory manager allocates memory to requesting processes until there is no more memory available or until there are no more processes waiting for memory.
